incident-bot: P1 — Acadia (enterprise / VPC tenant) incident triggered for eu-west-1: elevated 5xx, sporadic model timeouts. Pages sent to oncall.

Marie Chen: Oncall here. Seeing spike in 5xx for tenant acadia-prod originating in eu-west-1. Dashboard: latency up, errors \u003e 15%. Confirming customer impact — Luis, can you confirm if Acadia is seeing user-facing errors?

Luis Ortega: Yep, their SRE just pinged our CS contact — some API requests failing with 502s and long stalls. They reported intermittent failures starting ~T-18m. No full outage yet but error rate high.

David Li: I'm seeing backend health checks flapping on the dedicated-eu-west pool for acadia. kube probes failing on a subset of pods. Error patterns: OOM-ish logs then restart loop for a small host group.

Julia Kim: Logs show heavy KV cache thrash during a spike of long-context requests for this tenant. Possible memory/eviction pressure on the dedicated warm cache instance.

Marie Chen: Immediate plan: 1) Quarantine tenant from shared pools so we avoid noisy neighbors, 2) Shift traffic off the failing eu-west warm nodes into the reserved warm & fallback region (eu-central), 3) If necessary, perform DNS cutover to the dedicated-warm endpoint.

Ashok Patel: +1. I'll start the quarantine and open a temporary route to eu-central warm. Marie — you want me to lower DNS TTL ahead of cutover?

Marie Chen: Yes, lower TTL to 60s for acadia-prod.redwood.example.com before any DNS change. Luis — can your edge team accept a brief TTL change?

Luis Ortega: We can handle TTL change. Will coordinate on our side. Go ahead.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Record: rolling config change submitted: "tenant-quarantine: acadia-prod -> block shared-pool" by Ashok Patel.

Ashok Patel: Running quarantine command now: 

```
rwctl tenant quarantine acadia-prod --scope shared-pool --reason "increased 5xx and cache thrash" --by ashok
```

Ashok Patel: quarantine applied. New session routing should avoid shared-pool for new connections. Existing sessions are sticky — leaving them active for now.

David Li: Checking warm pool capacity: 

```
rwctl pool status --pool acadia-dedicated-warm-eu1
# output: total_slots: 8, active_slots: 5, warm_reserved: 4, free_warm: 3
```

David Li: We have 3 free warm slots. I'll provision an extra warm instance from eu-central as standby.

Julia Kim: Spinning up warm replica in eu-central: 

```
rwctl pool scale --pool acadia-dedicated-warm-eu-central --replicas +1
```

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Scaling request accepted. Provisioning new slice (id slice-7321). Estimated ready in ~4m.

Marie Chen: Lowering DNS TTL to 60 now (affects acadia-prod).

Ashok Patel: TTL change issued: 

```
# Route53 API
change_resource_record_sets --change-batch '{"Comment":"lower TTL for acadia cutover","Changes":[{"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"acadia-prod.redwood.example.com","Type":"CNAME","TTL":60,"ResourceRecords":[{"Value":"acadia-prod.edge.redwood.example.com"}]}}]}'
```

Ashok Patel: TTL lowered. Confirmed via dig: 

```
$ dig +short acadia-prod.redwood.example.com
acadia-prod.edge.redwood.example.com.
;; TTL: 60
```

Luis Ortega: Their edge team confirmed they see TTL=60. Ready to accept a staged shift.

Marie Chen: Next: staged traffic shift. We'll route 20% of new sessions to eu-central warm (slice-7321) and 80% remain in eu-west routing to other healthy nodes. Watch error rate and p99 latency.

Ashok Patel: Applying traffic policy: 

```
rwctl routing update --tenant acadia-prod --policy '{"rules":[{"region":"eu-west-1","weight":80},{"region":"eu-central-1","weight":20}]}'
```

David Li: Policy applied. Monitoring metrics stream.

Julia Kim: After ~2 mins: errors dropped from 15% -> 6% for acadia. P95 latency improved ~200ms. Some old sessions still fail (sticky), but new sessions look much better.

Luis Ortega: Customer reports a big reduction in visible errors for most users. They still see occasional failures for long-lived sessions. Any plan for those?

Marie Chen: For stubborn sticky sessions we can trigger a graceful session drain on failing nodes. Plan: mark problematic nodes in eu-west as draining (no new sessions) and let sessions expire or migrate with reauth.

Ashok Patel: Initiating drain on pods with restart loop: 

```
kubectl annotate pod pod-9382 evict=drain --namespace acadia-prod
kubectl cordon node node-az1-eu-west
```

David Li: Drains in progress. Restart loops stopped after eviction; some pods recovered with cleared cache. Observed drop in OOM-like logs.

Marie Chen: Good. Once drain stabilizes, shift weight to eu-central until eu-west is healthy again. If we need full failover, we'll swap DNS CNAME to point to dedicated warm endpoint in eu-central and set weights accordingly.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: slice-7321 is ready (eu-central warm).

Ashok Patel: Increasing eu-central weight to 60% now to accelerate recovery and protect against further eu-west flaps.

David Li: After increase: error rate down to 1.8%, latency stable. No new restarts observed on eu-west after drains.

Luis Ortega: We're good on customer side. They want a short maintenance note to their users, but prefer no full DNS swap yet.

Marie Chen: Agreed. We'll keep staged routing and monitor for 30m. If stable, we'll close incident. If any regression, we'll proceed with full DNS cutover and tenant-specific CNAME pointing to eu-central dedicated warm.

Ashok Patel: Logging handoff — I'm taking the next 30m oncall watch to monitor and own the rollback if needed. Marie — handing off incident control to Ashok.

Marie Chen: Acknowledged. Ashok has control. Posting summary for postmortem: root cause likely cache eviction thrash under a workload spike leading to OOM/restarts on a warm host subset. Action items: 1) Improve KV cache eviction policies for enterprise tenants, 2) Add proactive warm margin checks when QPS spikes for long-context workloads, 3) Update runbook to include TTL change steps and customer edge coordination.

Ashok Patel: Noted. I'm keeping the quarantine active until we confirm zero restarts for 45m. Current metrics stable.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: impact reduced. Status: Mitigated. Assigned to: Ashok Patel for monitoring and post-incident writeup.

David Li: I'll grab logs and create an artifact tarball for the postmortem: /artifacts/incidents/2479991111-acadia-cache-thrash.tar.gz

Luis Ortega: Thanks team — customer contact sent a short note to their users acknowledging a partial degradation and thanking us for the quick mitigation.

Marie Chen: Thanks all. I'll open the postmortem ticket and schedule a follow-up with Research/Runtime and Product to discuss cache policy changes. Marking thread: monitored -> resolved if stable for the next 30m. :white_check_mark:
